newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Illegal home of Arab bomb victim spared demolition.
newsitem.headline: Illegal home of Arab bomb victim spared demolition.

text.p: Just two weeks after suicide bombers nearly killed his son, Abdel-Rahman Khader found Israeli authorities trying to bulldoze the house he was building for his family of 12.
His lawyer got the order delayed -- at least temporarily.
"I don't know if they sympathise with my son or if they sympathise with me or what," Khader, 38, said as he stood on the foundations of his new home in East Jerusalem.
Around him lay a mangled concrete and steel mess which used to be the start of five other homes.
Israel destroyed nine Arab houses it said were illegally built near Shuafat and Bethlehem on Wednesday. It was going to destroy the Khader home for the same reason.
"I need the house. It's not a great house, just one or two bedrooms. I want it for my son. I want my son to live in it because he is (now) handicapped," he said.
"For humanitarian reasons the municipality will suspend the demolition and pass it to the courts," a city spokeswoman said.

Khader said he hoped to move into the new home with his wife and 10 children from a one-bedroom apartment in the Shuafat refugee camp. But rights groups said they expected the Khader home would eventually be destroyed.
Khader's 15-year-old son Saad lost his leg in a double suicide attack in Jerusalem's Mahane Yehuda market on July 30 that claimed the lives of 14 people and the two bombers.
"They amputated his leg from here," said Khader, pointing to a spot above the knee. "His body was burnt. When I saw the scene, I was confused, I was crying."
"I'm very tired and I don't know what to do," he said.
Rights groups accuse Israel of using last month's suicide bombing as a cover for carrying out demolitions.
"I think they're using the bombing and the international response to carry out their activities," said Jennifer Moorehead of the Palestinian civil rights group LAW.

The municipality said it had destroyed eight Jerusalem homes since the bombing, compared to only one in the previous seven months. Israel's military-run Civil Administration has also destroyed at least nine West Bank homes in the past two weeks.
A municipality spokeswoman said some of the demolitions were planned before the bombing and followed a long court process.
Palestinians say they are forced to build illegally because the municipality will not give them permits. They accuse Israel of trying to drive them out of Jerusalem.
Palestinians want East Jerusalem as capital of a future state. Israel calls the city its undivided eternal capital.
